The product rule for double summations states that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{b}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{j}.
$$

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{\sum }_{j=1}^{11}{a}_{i}({b}_{j}-6) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{11}({b}_{j}-6).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{11}({b}_{j}-6) & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{a}_{i})\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{11}{b}_{j}-{\sum }_{j=1}^{11}6) \\  & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{a}_{i})\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{11}{b}_{j}-6{\sum }_{j=1}^{11}1) \\  & =(15)\cdot (68-6\cdot 11) \\  & =(15)\cdot (68-66) \\  & =(15)\cdot (2) \\  & =30\end{aligned}
$$
